question.problem: The inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{{8}^{6x}}{3}$ is ${f}^{-1}(x)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{8}^{6x}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{8}^{6y}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{8}^{6y}}{3} \\ 3x & ={8}^{6y} \\ {log}_{8}⁡(3x) & ={log}_{8}⁡({8}^{6y}) \\ {log}_{8}⁡(3x) & =6y \\ 6y & ={log}_{8}⁡(3x) \\ y & =\frac{{log}_{8}⁡(3x)}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{{log}_{8}⁡(3x)}{6}.$
